# BOARD

<!-- Generated by tools/board.py render --repo from the work-item issues: change an issue, not a row. -->

Index of the live work packages, one row per open `work-item` issue. Each row links its brief in `briefs/<ID>.md` where one exists; the State column is last and starts with one of: `queued` → `building` → `in review` → `merged` | `escalated` | `dropped`, optionally followed by a short note in parentheses. To add or change a row, open or edit its issue (title `<ID>: <package>`, a `board-row` block, a `state:` label; tools/board.py); merged and dropped rows leave the board, and those before 2026-10-10 are in [docs/BOARD-HISTORY.md](docs/BOARD-HISTORY.md). Detail goes in the brief, not the row (docs/OPERATING.md §5). A row's finding class is its `class:` label: `class:release` rows are what the first release needs.

The board follows the capability-kernel migration (D-139, [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) §3). Step 0 (freeze) and step 1 (SPEC v1.0) are merged. The first section lists the remaining steps in order: MIG-2 builds the kernel, MIG-3 the first slice, MIG-4 the ports by directory and MIG-5 deletes the old core. A step's row opens its detail rows only when the step starts, from SPEC v1.0 IDs (Appendix A maps each retired ID). The other sections hold the work on parts that survive the migration, grouped by the SPEC v1.0 section they serve; open issues the migration supersedes are closed with a reason citing PLAN.md §3, so no row names a retired phase or a retired ID family.

## Harness and operating model

| ID | Package | Needs | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| RT-2 | Risk-tier follow-ups from PR #705's reviews (brief to write): CI and reviewers compute the tier with the base branch's `tools/risk_tier.py`, not the PR's own copy (invariant: a PR cannot edit the rules that set its review depth; failure: a PR drops `image/` from the A list and edits a unit, and both runs print B); `tools/hostcheck*` to A (HOST-1e; failure: a C PR allow-lists a real host change and the HW-8 check reports it as disclosed) | RT-1 | building |
| BASELINE-prune | BASELINE-prune: Remove the 12 stale hashes from `tests/product_name_baseline.json`. The baseline should only shrink. (later; tier B; from PR #1811) | — | queued (later; tier B; from PR #1811) |
| BOARD-transition-relation | BOARD-transition-relation: add a transition relation to `tools/board.py` (reject merged→anything and →merged with no merged PR), enforced in `board.yml`. (later; tier C; from state-machine audit R9) | — | queued (later; tier C; from state-machine audit R9) |
| STALEQ-closes-f1 | `tools/stalequeued.py` only sees open issues (`board.work_items` uses `state=open`), and GitHub auto-closes an issue when a PR with `Closes #N` merges to main. So the `closed by PR #N` line fires mostly when the row was reopened after that PR merged (more owed), or the keyword was added after merge, and a dispatcher then skips a live row. Option: report `closes` only when the PR merged after the issue's last reopen (issue events), else `maybe: reopened after PR #M` (later, recheck; L3 on #2255). | STALEQ-closes | queued |
| OPS-budget-pointer | Budget skill pointer gets the Read fallback; docs citing CLAUDE.md §Budget point at the skill | MIG-1 | queued (C; gate files; after #2523) |
